articles.title: EXPLAINER | Why is SA experiencing such intense heat in spring? - Sowetan

articles.full_text:
While El Niño is associated with hotter and drier conditions, whether the intensity of the current heat is normal for early spring remains debatable, says weather forecaster Lehlohonolo Thobela.
South Africans sweltering under hot spring temperatures may be wondering why it is so hot and whether these conditions are normal for this time of the year.
The SA Weather Services (SAWS) has issued a warning regarding hot conditions expected around the country this weekend.
Thobela said the current hot and dry conditions were consistent with the influence of El Niño, a natural climate phenomenon that can influence weather patterns across Southern Africa.
Thobela said seasonal forecasts pointed to above-normal minimum and maximum temperatures, alongside below-normal rainfall as the country moves towards summer.
“The main thing now is that we are in spring, and obviously there are high temperatures,” he said.
He explained that the weather patterns expected over the coming months were consistent with El Niño, which is commonly associated with hotter and drier conditions in SA’s summer rainfall regions.
Thobela said El Niño was a natural climate phenomenon characterised by warmer than usual sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
Thobela said SA could experience more hot and dry conditions as the phenomenon developed over the coming months. “We are expecting an El Niño effect that will get stronger.”
He noted that although temperatures generally rose during spring as the country transitioned from winter to summer, the intensity of the current heat raised questions about whether such conditions were normal this early in the season.
Thobela said while current conditions were consistent with the expected characteristics of El Niño, he cautioned against determining whether the intensity of the heat was normal, something which required further research into historical temperature patterns.
“To say it’s normal for us to have such heat so early in spring could be debatable,” he said.
Thobela said the seasonal outlook pointed to continued above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall as the country approached summer.
The weather service said the country should expect more hot conditions, isolated thunderstorms and possible cooler weather in some coastal areas this weekend.
Heatwaves are expected to persist in parts of northern KwaZulu-Natal until Sunday and Mpumalanga until Monday.
Gauteng is expected to experience partly cloudy and warm conditions, with isolated showers and thundershowers. It will be hot in the province’s extreme northern areas.
Isolated afternoon showers and thunderstorms are also possible in parts of Mpumalanga, Limpopo, North West and the Free State.
The service also warned of extremely high fire-danger conditions across parts of the Northern Cape, Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Free State, KwaZulu-Natal, Mpumalanga and Limpopo.
Residents are urged to drink plenty of water, avoid strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest parts of the day and ensure vulnerable people have access to shade and water. The public should also exercise caution when handling open flames and monitor weather warnings for updates.

articles.title: Orange alert issued for İstanbul as heavy rainfall expected tonight - Bianet

articles.full_text:
The General Directorate of Meteorology (MGM) issued an orange weather alert for İstanbul as heavy rainfall is expected to begin tonight and tomorrow.
As of 7 pm local time (GMT+3), heavy rainfall of 21 to 50 kilograms per square meter is expected in parts of the city.
Rainfall is forecast to intensify from tomorrow afternoon, particularly on the Asian side, with some areas expected to receive between 50 and 100 kilograms per square meter.
The directorate warned that the downpours could trigger flooding, flash floods and landslides, as well as disruptions to transportation.
Residents were urged to remain cautious and take precautions against the potential effects of the severe weather.
The weather warning will remain in place until 5 am on Oct 18.
İstanbul has been experiencing severe rainfall since late Oct 13, which caused flooding across the city. At least five people lost their lives in the floods and several others are still missing.
